title: Despite "super-human” performance, current LLMs are unsuited for decisions about ethics and safety

bias_targets.methodology: Rewording common-sense ethical scenarios with semantically neutral but statistically loaded features (e.g., "dangerous-sounding" or "helpful-sounding" language) to evaluate how models rely on surface-level lexical heuristics rather than actual ethical reasoning.

Applying prompt perturbations and analyzing chain-of-thought rationales to reveal that language models hallucinate justifications based on statistical artifacts from their pre-training data rather than the semantics of the prompt.
Manually categorizing human disagreements with the ETHICS dataset ground-truth labels to quantify how often varying ethical judgments stem from cultural differences among annotators.
